levels.agentic: Agents choose each slot and steer the search: an agent coordinator, a strategist that meets more often with wider bounds and asks first for nothing, three proposals per slot. Code still keeps the budget, the floor on new designs, the frozen problem and the records. The most agent calls of the three.
levels.guided: Code runs the schedule and a strategist may change its course within the bounds you set. The middle.
levels.harnessed: Code decides where the search goes: the schedule picks each slot, there is no strategist, settings moves are drawn by code, one proposal per slot. Agents write the designs and the lessons. The fewest agent calls of the three.

run_types.custom: Your own choices. Describe the search in `run.description`; where you set nothing, the guidance for the size of the budget and then the defaults apply.
run_types.discovery: Long runs with cheap evaluations, aiming for something unusual. Architecture and recipe both open, novelty high, the lightest harness.
run_types.explore_then_exploit: Most searches. Mostly new designs for the first 60% of the budget, then mostly local work and crossover on what was found.
run_types.refine: A known good model. Few lineages, mostly local moves, the overall shape of the model kept.
run_types.settings_only: A hyperparameter search. No structure changes; every slot is a settings move.
run_types.survey: A new problem. Mostly new designs throughout, kept on an archive so each kind stays in play.

skills: No skill: the run type and the defaults decide.
skills.algorithm-runtime: the same results in less time or memory
skills.bioinformatics-algorithm: better accuracy against a truth set, at an acceptable run time
skills.data-pipeline: the same output from a pipeline in less time, memory or cost
skills.model-distillation: a smaller or faster model that matches a larger model or an ensemble
skills.model-efficiency: the same score at a lower cost in parameters or time
skills.model-ensemble-members: a set of strong models whose errors do not coincide
skills.model-finetuning: the best score on a task starting from a pretrained model
skills.model-mechanistic: a better fit without losing what the parameters mean
skills.model-performance: the best score, nothing else weighed
skills.model-size-frontier: the best model at every size or speed across a broad range
skills.model-training-recipe: a better score from the same architecture, by training it better
skills.settings-tuning: the best values for the settings of fixed code

spaces.architecture_and_recipe: Every marked block is open: the model and the recipe (the roles in `space.recipe_roles`).
spaces.custom: Only what `space.roles` opens, role by role: {role: open | settings | fixed}.
spaces.module: Only the structure blocks whose role or name is listed in `space.modules`, and the params blocks.
spaces.open_architecture: Every model block is open; the training recipe is fixed.
spaces.template: Every model block is open, and writers are told to keep the overall shape of the baseline.

strategies.archive: The best of each kind of design on a grid (by family and size). Parents are drawn across the grid, the less visited cells favoured in proportion to `schedule.novelty`.
strategies.greedy: Always build on the current best (or one tied with it within the noise). The right choice when the budget is too small for a population.
strategies.lineage: Species kept alive side by side. A new lineage gets a protected trial, the best few are active, none takes more than its quota of the local slots, and one that stops gaining retires to the bench.
strategies.pareto: Build on the designs that are best on the score and a second figure at once (`strategy.second_metric`: size, speed, or a metric the runs report). Parents come from that trade-off front, the designs standing alone on it favoured; a crossover pairs designs from different parts of it.
strategies.tournament: Draw a few of the most recent designs and build on the best of them. Older designs leave the population however good they were, so one lucky score cannot dominate for long.

warnings: for about 30 evaluations the guidance suggests the greedy strategy; this run uses lineage

the skill needs: the training script must produce the teacher's outputs (or read stored ones) and train the student against them; the loss and augmentation blocks should be marked as open recipe blocks
the skill needs: to rank on speed or size, report `parameters` and `inference_speed.examples_per_s` in result.json; then `strategy.mechanism: pareto` or `limits` can use them
the skill needs: if the teacher is an ensemble, add a reference row for the ensemble and one for its best single member
the search space is wide (architecture and recipe) for 30 evaluations

the skill needs: report `parameters` in result.json (and `inference_speed.examples_per_s` to rank on speed: then set strategy.second_metric to examples_per_s and strategy.second_direction to maximize)
the skill needs: set `limits` for the largest size or lowest speed you accept, and put those figures in the first progress line so that a design outside them costs seconds
the skill needs: add a reference row for the model you are trying to shrink
for about 30 evaluations the guidance suggests the greedy strategy; this run uses pareto
the skill needs: report `signature` in result.json: a list of numbers saying where the model's errors fall (per class, per range of the target, or per held-out example); the groups are made from it
the skill needs: after the search, score the average of the best design of each group yourself; evoloop does not train or score ensembles
for about 30 evaluations the guidance suggests the greedy strategy; this run uses archive
behaviour is measured from `signature` in result.json: an adapter that does not report it gets no behaviour grouping
an archive needs many designs to fill; with 30 evaluations most cells will hold one model
the skill needs: load the pretrained weights from a fixed path outside base/ (weights are not copied per design)
the skill needs: mark as open the head, the choice of what is frozen, and the optimizer settings; leave the backbone's definition closed
the skill needs: add a reference row for the frozen backbone with a linear head

the skill needs: optional, and worth doing: report a figure of how well the parts match what is known (the share of filters matching known motifs, recovered interactions, parameters within physical ranges) under diagnostics; it can then be a leaderboard column, a speciality metric, or the second figure of the pareto strategy
the skill needs: report `signature` (where the errors fall) so that designs with the same failure are told apart from ones that fail differently
the skill needs: mark as open only the blocks that define the interpretable parts and their combination; leave the data handling and the evaluation frozen
the skill needs: report `parameters` in result.json for every design; the bands are made from it
the skill needs: to band by speed instead, report `inference_speed.examples_per_s` and set strategy.descriptors to the name of that metric under diagnostics
the skill needs: set `limits` for the smallest and largest size worth having, so that designs outside the range are not trained
the skill needs: mark the loss, optimizer, schedule and augmentation as blocks with those roles; the model blocks stay closed
the skill needs: report the training score beside the validation score under diagnostics, so that fitting and generalising can be told apart
the skill needs: report `best_epoch` and `epochs_run` in result.json
the skill needs: compare every design's output with a stored reference output and write `valid: false` with `rejected: "output differs"` when it does not match (exactly, or within a stated tolerance)

the skill needs: time the run several times on a quiet machine with a fixed number of threads, and report the median as the score with objective.direction minimize; set evaluation.noise from the spread of repeats
the skill needs: keep a second set of inputs the search never sees, and report its timing under diagnostics.hidden
the skill needs: report peak memory under diagnostics if it matters, and bound it with `limits`

the skill needs: score against a truth set with a standard comparison for the task, and report precision, recall and their combination under diagnostics; the score should be one number that does not reward trading one for the other at a single threshold
the skill needs: use more than one dataset (another sample, depth or organism), and keep one the search never sees under diagnostics.hidden
the skill needs: check the output's format and coordinates before scoring, and write `valid: false` with the reason when they are wrong
the skill needs: report run time and peak memory under diagnostics, and bound them with `limits` if they matter

the skill needs: run the pipeline on fixed sample data and compare its output with a stored reference (a checksum of sorted records, or row counts with value checks); write `valid: false` with the reason when it differs
the skill needs: report the cost as the score with objective.direction minimize: wall time as a median of repeats, or a figure that combines time and memory if both matter
the skill needs: report time per step and peak memory under diagnostics, so that the agents can see where the cost is
the skill needs: use sample data large enough that input and output costs resemble the real run, and keep a second sample the search never sees under diagnostics.hidden
the skill needs: every setting to tune must sit in a marked params block (one dict of numbers, true/false or text)
the skill needs: give bounds for settings that must stay in a range with `space.ranges`, e.g. {"fit.lr": [0.00001, 0.1]}; without one a setting may move a hundredfold either way
the skill needs: to stop poor settings early, report progress and set `evaluation.ladder`
block swap needs at least two open structure blocks; this search space may have one
